sections.title: Introduction to Speed Maths
sections.content: Simplification tests your ability to solve complex mathematical equations rapidly. The foundational pillars for this topic are memoization: you must memorize tables up to 20, squares up to 40, cubes up to 20, and fractional percentage values up to 1/20.

sections.title: The VBODMAS Rule
sections.content: The absolute rule for solving any equation. V = Vinculum (Bar bracket), B = Brackets (), {}, [], O = Of (Multiplication), D = Division, M = Multiplication, A = Addition, S = Subtraction. Always solve strictly from left to right when operations have the same priority.

sections.title: Fraction to Percentage Conversions
sections.content: Memorize base fractions to speed up calculations. 1/2 = 50%, 1/3 = 33.33%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%, 1/6 = 16.66%, 1/7 = 14.28%, 1/8 = 12.5%, 1/9 = 11.11%, 1/11 = 9.09%. Use these to replace decimals in the exam.

sections.title: Basic Algebraic Identities
sections.content: Frequently, big numbers are disguised as algebraic formulas. Memorize: (a+b)² = a² + b² + 2ab; (a-b)² = a² + b² - 2ab; a² - b² = (a-b)(a+b); (a+b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a+b).

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Ignoring the 'Of' operation and performing Division first (Of always comes before Division). 2. Adding before multiplying due to reading left-to-right without applying BODMAS. 3. Calculating exact values when an approximation is required.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 1 is about strict adherence to VBODMAS and utilizing memorized values (squares, cubes, fraction-percentages) to bypass manual calculation. Never violate the operational hierarchy.

tricks.title: Percentage Swap Rule
tricks.explanation: A% of B is exactly equal to B% of A. Use this when one number is easier to calculate as a percentage.
tricks.example: Find 32% of 25. Swap it: 25% of 32 = 1/4 of 32 = 8. Solved in 2 seconds.

tricks.title: Multiplication by 11
tricks.explanation: To multiply a 2-digit number by 11, separate the two digits and place their sum in the middle.
tricks.example: 45 x 11. Separate 4 and 5. 4 + 5 = 9. Answer is 495. If the sum > 9, carry over the 1 (e.g., 85 x 11 = 8(13)5 = 935).

tricks.title: Multiplication by 5, 25, 125
tricks.explanation: Instead of multiplying, use division. x 5 = (x * 10)/2. x 25 = (x * 100)/4. x 125 = (x * 1000)/8.

tricks.title: The 'a² - b²' Simplifier
tricks.explanation: If you see a difference of two squares, never calculate the squares. Add them and subtract them.
